title: Ancient Trees in Mexico: 3 Cities to Explore
meta_description: Mexico's oldest trees are mostly ahuehuetes, the national tree; El Arbol del Tule outside Oaxaca has the widest trunk on Earth. Three cities, 11 trees.
intro: Mexico's classified trees keep returning to one species: the ahuehuete, Taxodium mucronatum, sacred to the Aztecs and now the country's national tree. El Arbol del Tule outside Oaxaca carries the widest trunk of any tree on Earth, so wide that botanists once assumed it had to be several trunks fused together, until DNA testing in the 1990s proved it a single individual. Seven more ahuehuetes stand scattered across Mexico City's older parks and squares, planted in colonial-era courtyards and still growing wherever the water table lets them. Chiapa de Corzo's town square was built around a different giant, a kapok already standing when the Spanish founded the settlement in 1528. Between them, a country whose oldest trees were mostly there first, with the cities built to fit around them.
